### 3.4. Placing an Order

An order begins with a `Customer` issuing a placement request carrying three fields: the customer's own `customer_id`, the target `restaurant_id`, and an `items` array. Each entry in `items` specifies a `menu_item_id`, a snapshot `name` taken from the menu item at placement, a `unit_price_cents` pinned from the same snapshot, and a `quantity` of 1 or more. `items` must be non-empty. The order fails placement with `ERR_ORDER_INVALID` when `items` is empty, any quantity is below 1, or the resulting subtotal would be below 100 cents (the minimum order size). The target `Restaurant` must be `ACTIVE` and every `MenuItem` referenced must carry `is_listed` true and match the `Order.restaurant_id` — otherwise placement is rejected with `ERR_RESTAURANT_UNAVAILABLE`.

When placement succeeds, the server computes six derived fields atomically. `subtotal_cents` is the sum across `items` of `unit_price_cents` multiplied by `quantity`. `distance_km` is the haversine great-circle distance from the restaurant's coordinates (`lat`, `lng`) to the customer's coordinates (`lat`, `lng`), expressed in kilometres and rounded to one decimal place. `is_peak` is set to true when the placement moment falls inside one of the two peak windows defined in §2.10 and frozen on the order at that moment. `promised_delivery_time` is set to the placement time plus 45 minutes.

`provisional_delivery_fee_cents` is the solo-rider estimate of what the customer will pay for delivery. It is computed as a base of 300 cents, plus a per-kilometer surcharge of 120 cents for each whole kilometer band — where the band count is obtained by taking the ceiling of `distance_km` (so a 2.0-km distance produces 2 bands, while a 2.01-km distance produces 3 bands) and multiplying by 120, plus a peak surcharge of 200 cents whenever `is_peak` is true and zero cents otherwise. The provisional estimate does not model route merging, because merging is a runtime decision made only once a rider's current route is known.

`provisional_commission_cents` is the tiered platform commission, priced at placement time. The tier structure is marginal: the first 20 000 cents of `subtotal_cents` is billed at 15%, the portion of the subtotal strictly between 20 000 and 50 000 cents is billed at 18%, and any portion above 50 000 cents is billed at 22%. The computation proceeds in a fixed evaluation order — first the tier-1 amount is determined as the minimum of `subtotal_cents` and 20 000, then the tier-2 amount as the excess over 20 000 up to 50 000, then the tier-3 amount as any further excess. Each tier's amount is multiplied by its rate, the three products are summed in decimal, and only the final sum is rounded half-up to a whole cent. Rounding each tier independently and then summing is forbidden because it produces a different answer on boundary subtotals.

Order placement also authorizes payment. `payment_status` starts at `UNPAID` and immediately moves to `AUTHORIZED` as a placement-time side effect; any available `credit_balance_cents` on the customer is drawn down before the card authorization covers the remaining amount. `final_delivery_fee_cents`, `final_commission_cents`, `actual_delivery_time`, and `minutes_late` all start as null and are populated only when the order reaches `DELIVERED`. `version` starts at 1, as for every other versioned resource.

### 3.5. Restaurant-Side Order Flow

A restaurant that owns the target order can accept it, transitioning the order from `PLACED` to `RESTAURANT_ACCEPTED`. Acceptance is only legal while the restaurant's own `status` is `ACTIVE` and the order is still in `PLACED`; the restaurant identity is enforced by the `X-User-ID` match against `Order.restaurant_id`. Acceptance does not touch `payment_status` — the order is already `AUTHORIZED` from placement. From `RESTAURANT_ACCEPTED`, the restaurant signals start-preparing, advancing the order to `PREPARING`; this same action opens a dispatch offer to the best available rider, which may — depending on the current rider's route — merge into an existing `RouteGroup`. From `PREPARING`, the restaurant marks the order ready, advancing it to `READY_FOR_PICKUP`. Ready is only legal when a rider has already `ACCEPTED` the dispatch (or is further along at `PICKED_UP`) — the system refuses the ready transition otherwise with `ERR_INVALID_STATE`.

Either the customer or the restaurant (via rejection) may cancel an order while it is still in `PLACED`; the cancellation transitions the order to `CANCELLED` and moves `payment_status` from whichever of `UNPAID` or `AUTHORIZED` it is currently in to `VOIDED`. No charge has captured, so `credit_balance_cents` is not affected. `CustomerService` may also cancel on behalf of a customer. Cancellation once the order has moved beyond `PLACED` is not available through this channel; disputes at later stages flow through the refund workflow in §3.9.

The full set of `Order.status` values is `PLACED`, `RESTAURANT_ACCEPTED`, `PREPARING`, `READY_FOR_PICKUP`, `PICKED_UP`, `DELIVERED`, `CANCELLED`, `REFUND_REQUESTED`, and `REFUNDED`; the terminal states are `DELIVERED`, `CANCELLED`, and `REFUNDED`. The full set of `payment_status` values is `UNPAID`, `AUTHORIZED`, `CAPTURED`, `PARTIALLY_REFUNDED`, `FULLY_REFUNDED`, and `VOIDED`.

### 3.6. Dispatch, Assignment, and Route Merging

When a restaurant starts preparing an order, the system opens a dispatch offer — an `Assignment` row linking an `order_id` to a candidate `rider_id`. An assignment begins in `OFFERED` at its `offered_at` timestamp and evolves through `ACCEPTED`, `PICKED_UP`, and `DELIVERED` in the success path, or `REJECTED` / `CANCELLED` on abandonment. The full set of `Assignment.status` values is `OFFERED`, `ACCEPTED`, `PICKED_UP`, `DELIVERED`, `REJECTED`, and `CANCELLED`; `DELIVERED`, `REJECTED`, and `CANCELLED` are terminal.

The candidate `rider_id` is selected deterministically from the pool of riders whose `status` is `AVAILABLE` or `ON_DELIVERY`. Any rider currently linked to an `OFFERED`, `ACCEPTED`, or `PICKED_UP` `Assignment` for the same `order_id` is excluded from this pool up front — the system never re-offers an order to a rider who already holds it, regardless of whether the offer originated from `/start-preparing`, from an explicit `/dispatch`, or from the fresh offer the system issues after a rejection or cancellation. From the surviving candidates the system prefers any rider in `ON_DELIVERY` whose existing `ACTIVE` `RouteGroup` already contains at least one unpicked assignment whose pickup restaurant is within 500 metres of the new order's pickup restaurant — these are precisely the riders for whom acceptance would trigger the route-merge rule described two paragraphs below — over any rider in `AVAILABLE`. Within either preference tier the tie-breaker is `Rider.created_at` descending, so that the most recently registered rider wins; should that still tie, the rider whose `id` sorts lexicographically smallest is chosen. The presence of other live `Assignment` rows for the same `order_id` — including one already in `ACCEPTED` or `PICKED_UP` — is not by itself grounds for refusal; `/dispatch` always creates a new `OFFERED` `Assignment` so long as the pool is non-empty, and the uniqueness constraint stated in the next paragraph fires later at `/accept` time rather than at dispatch time. The dispatch is refused with `409 ERR_INVALID_STATE` only when the resulting candidate pool is empty, in which case no new `Assignment` is created.

Acceptance by a rider requires that the rider's current `status` be `AVAILABLE` or `ON_DELIVERY` (the latter is what enables route merging), that the corresponding `Order.status` be `RESTAURANT_ACCEPTED`, `PREPARING`, or `READY_FOR_PICKUP`, and — critically — that no other `Assignment` already exists for the same `order_id` in `OFFERED`, `ACCEPTED`, or `PICKED_UP`. When two riders race to accept the same dispatched offer, first-writer-wins on this uniqueness constraint: exactly one assignment advances to `ACCEPTED`, and the losing attempt is rejected with `ERR_ORDER_ALREADY_ASSIGNED`. Acceptance stamps `accepted_at`, cascades the rider's `status` to `ON_DELIVERY` if they were `AVAILABLE`, and triggers a recomputation of `acceptance_rate` over the rider's last 30 offers.

Route merging happens at the same moment. When the accepting rider already holds an `ACTIVE` `RouteGroup` and the newly accepted order's pickup restaurant is within 500 metres of an existing unpicked assignment's pickup restaurant, the new assignment is attached to that `RouteGroup` — its `route_group_id` is set to the group's `id` and the group's `assignment_ids` array is extended to include the new assignment's `id`. The `RouteGroup` itself tracks its own `rider_id`, `assignment_ids`, `merged_at` timestamp, and `status`, which spans `ACTIVE`, `COMPLETED`, and `ABANDONED`, starting in `ACTIVE`. Solo deliveries leave `route_group_id` null.

Rejection of an offer — either explicitly by the rider, or via the 60-second offer-timeout sweep that runs as part of the clock-advance capability — moves the assignment to `REJECTED`, recomputes the rider's `acceptance_rate`, and spawns a fresh `Assignment` for the order targeting the next best available rider.

Pickup advances the assignment from `ACCEPTED` to `PICKED_UP`, stamps `picked_up_at`, and cascades the order from `READY_FOR_PICKUP` to `PICKED_UP`. A rider may also cancel an assignment after accepting it but before pickup; this transition is legal only while the assignment is in `ACCEPTED` and the order has not yet reached `PICKED_UP`. Cancellation creates a `Fine` whose subject is the rider and whose `reason` is `RIDER_NO_SHOW`, with `amount_cents` fixed at 500 — the flat no-show penalty. That fine in turn debits the rider's `wallet_balance_cents` by 500 cents and triggers a `bonus_tier` recomputation (this is the transitive chain: the assignment cancellation triggers the fine, and the fine's creation triggers the wallet debit and tier recompute). The system then dispatches a fresh offer for the same order to the next best rider.

### 3.7. Delivery and Fiscal Reconciliation

The final operational step is delivery. A rider whose assignment is in `PICKED_UP` and whose corresponding order is in `PICKED_UP` invokes the deliver capability. The assignment transitions to `DELIVERED`, `delivered_at` is stamped, and the order cascades to `DELIVERED` as well. A substantial chain of fiscal side-effects fires atomically on this cascade.

First, the order's `actual_delivery_time` is set to the current instant, and `minutes_late` is computed as the non-negative floor of the seconds between `actual_delivery_time` and `promised_delivery_time`, divided by 60. Early or on-time deliveries produce a `minutes_late` of zero.

Second, the order's `final_delivery_fee_cents` is reconciled from the frozen placement inputs. The solo-style fee is recomputed from the original `distance_km` and `is_peak` snapshots using the same base-of-300, 120-per-band, 200-peak formula as the provisional fee. Then, if the assignment carries a non-null `route_group_id` and its route group contains two or more assignments, a 25% route-merge discount is applied: the discount is computed as the floor of the solo fee times 0.25, and the rider-facing delivery fee is the solo fee minus that discount. Solo deliveries (no `route_group_id`, or a `RouteGroup` containing only this assignment) carry no discount and the final fee equals the solo fee. The reconciled amount is written to both `Order.final_delivery_fee_cents` and `Assignment.final_delivery_fee_cents` — these two mirror each other for any single-leg delivery, and for merged deliveries the platform absorbs the discount as a cost of bundling.

Third, the order's `final_commission_cents` is reconciled — and this is where it may diverge from `provisional_commission_cents`. If, at the moment of delivery, the owning restaurant's `commission_rate_override` is a non-null decimal, commission is computed as a flat rate: the subtotal multiplied by that override rate, rounded half-up to a whole cent. The override applies to the entire subtotal, not just the portion above any tier threshold. If `commission_rate_override` is null at delivery time, the same tiered formula described in §3.4 runs again — 15% / 18% / 22% across the same 20 000-cent and 50 000-cent caps, summed in decimal and then rounded half-up once. Because the override can be changed mid-flight by the restaurant or a `PlatformAdmin`, the final commission can legitimately differ from the provisional one even though the subtotal is immutable.

Fourth, `payment_status` moves unconditionally to `CAPTURED`.

Fifth, if `minutes_late` is greater than zero, a `Fine` is created whose subject is the rider and whose `reason` is `LATE_DELIVERY`. The fine amount is tiered: when `minutes_late` is from 1 through 10 inclusive, `amount_cents` is a flat 200 cents (a two-dollar penalty); when `minutes_late` is from 11 through 30 inclusive, `amount_cents` is 500 plus 50 per minute over 10 — so a 20-minute lateness yields 500 plus 50 times 10, which is 1 000 cents; when `minutes_late` exceeds 30, `amount_cents` is the smaller of `final_delivery_fee_cents` and 1 500 (the rider's earnings clawback is capped at $15 regardless of the fee) plus an additional 500 cents of customer compensation. This fine creation itself triggers a follow-on debit of the rider's `wallet_balance_cents` by `amount_cents` and a recomputation of the rider's `bonus_tier` — the same transitive fan-out chain as the no-show case.

Sixth, the owning restaurant's `pending_settlement_cents` is incremented by `subtotal_cents` minus `final_commission_cents` — the restaurant's slice of the order.

Seventh, the rider's `wallet_balance_cents` is credited with the reconciled `Assignment.final_delivery_fee_cents` (net of any merge discount absorbed by the platform) and the rider's `bonus_tier` is recomputed a final time for the delivery event.

Eighth, if the assignment belonged to a `RouteGroup` and every peer assignment in that group has also reached `DELIVERED`, the `RouteGroup` transitions from `ACTIVE` to `COMPLETED`. Otherwise the group stays `ACTIVE` and the rider stays `ON_DELIVERY`. A rider only returns to `AVAILABLE` once no active assignments remain for them.

All of these effects happen as part of the same request. A single rider delivery therefore mutates the assignment, the order, the restaurant, the rider, the fine (when created), and potentially the route group — and each versioned resource in that chain has its `updated_at` refreshed and its `version` incremented exactly once.

### 3.8. Restaurant Settlement

At each payout cycle, the platform settles with each `ACTIVE` restaurant. A `PlatformAdmin` invokes the restaurant's settle capability; the restaurant's `pending_settlement_cents` is reset to 0, and the settlement event is treated as the paid-out audit marker. Returns that were approved after a delivery but before the settlement cycle decrement `pending_settlement_cents` at the moment of approval (see §3.9); deliveries increment it. Because both updates are performed atomically as part of the triggering request, the running aggregate is always consistent with the set of `Order` rows in `DELIVERED` that have not been `FULLY_REFUNDED`. The aggregate is never recomputed from scratch; each event applies an incremental delta.

### 3.9. Returns and Refunds

A customer may open a return on a delivered order. The customer-facing payload carries the return's `reason` — one of `QUALITY_ISSUE`, `WRONG_ITEM`, `LATE`, or `OTHER` — and a `requested_refund_cents` amount. The request is only eligible when the order is in `DELIVERED` and the current moment is within 24 hours of the order's `actual_delivery_time`; requests outside that window are rejected with `ERR_RETURN_WINDOW_EXPIRED`. The requested refund must be at least 1 and at most the order's `subtotal_cents`; values out of range are rejected with `ERR_REFUND_AMOUNT_INVALID`. A duplicate return attempt — a request made while another `Return` for the same order is already in `REQUESTED`, `APPROVED`, or `ESCALATED` — is rejected with `ERR_DUPLICATE_RETURN`.

A successful return request creates a `Return` row in `REQUESTED` carrying the `order_id`, the `reason`, the `requested_refund_cents`, and — at decision time — the `reviewer_cs_user_id` that recorded the outcome. The owning `Order` transitions from `DELIVERED` to `REFUND_REQUESTED`. The full set of `Return.status` values is `REQUESTED`, `APPROVED`, `REJECTED`, and `ESCALATED`; `APPROVED` and `REJECTED` are terminal.

A `CustomerService` operator then reviews. Approval carries an `approved_refund_cents` amount that must be at least 1, at most the order's `subtotal_cents`, and at most the originally requested refund — any violation is rejected with `ERR_REFUND_AMOUNT_INVALID`. On approval, the `Return` moves to `APPROVED` and the owning order cascades from `REFUND_REQUESTED` to `REFUNDED`. The order's `payment_status` becomes `PARTIALLY_REFUNDED` if `approved_refund_cents` is strictly less than `subtotal_cents`, or `FULLY_REFUNDED` if the approved amount equals the subtotal. The customer's `credit_balance_cents` is credited by `approved_refund_cents`. The restaurant's `pending_settlement_cents` is decremented by the same amount. And finally, if the customer's `trust_score` is strictly below 0.5 and the return's `reason` is `QUALITY_ISSUE`, a `Fine` is created whose subject is the customer and whose `reason` is `ABUSIVE_RETURN` with `amount_cents` equal to `approved_refund_cents`. The four possible `Fine.reason` values are `LATE_DELIVERY`, `ABUSIVE_RETURN`, `RESTAURANT_STOCKOUT`, and `RIDER_NO_SHOW`; a fine's `subject_type` is one of `RIDER`, `RESTAURANT`, or `CUSTOMER` and its `subject_id` is the matching entity's `id`. A fine's `settlement_status` begins at `PENDING` and can move to `SETTLED` (when the underlying wallet or settlement event has cleared the balance) or `WAIVED` (when a `CustomerService` operator or `PlatformAdmin` forgives the debit and reverses any wallet or credit adjustment).

Rejection by a `CustomerService` operator moves the `Return` to `REJECTED` and reverts the order from `REFUND_REQUESTED` to `DELIVERED` with no monetary change. Escalation moves the `Return` from `REQUESTED` to `ESCALATED` and opens a `WorkOrder` linked via `related_return_id` for supervisor attention. An escalated return can be brought back to `REQUESTED` through a reopen step — this closes the linked `WorkOrder`. The approve / reject transitions accept both `REQUESTED` and `ESCALATED` as legal starting states; the reopen transition is only legal from `ESCALATED`.

### 3.10. Work Orders and Service Tickets

A `WorkOrder` is the platform's generic dispute-and-query artifact. Any of the five roles can open one, supplying `opened_by_role` (one of `CUSTOMER`, `RIDER`, `RESTAURANT`, or `CUSTOMER_SERVICE`), `opened_by_id` (the opener's identifier — a `Customer.id`, `Rider.id`, `Restaurant.id`, or opaque `CustomerService` operator id), a `category` drawn from `DELIVERY_LATE`, `FOOD_QUALITY`, `MISSING_ITEM`, `RIDER_BEHAVIOR`, `RESTAURANT_BEHAVIOR`, `PAYMENT_ISSUE`, or `OTHER`, and optionally a `related_order_id` referencing an `Order` or a `related_return_id` referencing a `Return`. `resolution_notes` starts null and is set when the ticket is resolved; `assigned_cs_user_id` starts null and is set when a CS operator claims the ticket.

The ticket opens in `OPEN`. A `CustomerService` operator (or `PlatformAdmin`) claims the ticket, recording `assigned_cs_user_id` as the caller and transitioning the ticket to `UNDER_REVIEW`. From `UNDER_REVIEW`, the operator can request additional information from the opener — the ticket advances to `AWAITING_INFO` — and the opener (a `Customer`, `Rider`, or `Restaurant`) responds by submitting info, which cycles the ticket back to `UNDER_REVIEW`. When the opener acts, their `X-User-ID` must match `opened_by_id`. From `UNDER_REVIEW` the operator may either escalate the ticket (`UNDER_REVIEW → ESCALATED`) or resolve it (`UNDER_REVIEW → RESOLVED`), and from `ESCALATED` the operator may resolve it as well (`ESCALATED → RESOLVED`). Resolving a ticket requires that `assigned_cs_user_id` be non-null, and — critically — if `related_return_id` is set, the linked `Return`'s `status` must be in `APPROVED` or `REJECTED` before the ticket can move to `RESOLVED`; attempting to resolve while the linked return is still `REQUESTED` or `ESCALATED` is rejected with `ERR_RELATED_RETURN_UNRESOLVED`. Resolution is the moment the operator records `resolution_notes`. From `RESOLVED` the ticket is closed (`RESOLVED → CLOSED`), which is terminal.

The full set of `WorkOrder.status` values is `OPEN`, `UNDER_REVIEW`, `AWAITING_INFO`, `RESOLVED`, `ESCALATED`, and `CLOSED`. A `Return` escalation opens a `WorkOrder` automatically, and that ticket is closed automatically when the return is reopened.

### 3.11. Fines and the Waive Mechanism

Every fine — whether it originated from a late delivery, a no-show assignment cancellation, an abusive return, or a restaurant stockout (the `RESTAURANT_STOCKOUT` reason) — is queryable by filtering on `subject_type`, `subject_id`, and `settlement_status`. A `Rider`, `Restaurant`, or `Customer` may query only their own fines; their `X-User-ID` must match the `subject_id` filter. `CustomerService` and `PlatformAdmin` may query any subject.

A `CustomerService` operator or `PlatformAdmin` may waive a `Fine` that is still in `PENDING`; waiving moves its `settlement_status` to `WAIVED` and reverses the fine's prior debit on the subject's ledger — a rider's `wallet_balance_cents` is credited back by `amount_cents`, a customer's credit balance is likewise restored, and a restaurant's pending settlement is returned to its pre-fine state. `SETTLED` fines are not waivable.

## 4. Endpoint Definitions

The general response-code convention is that operations which create a new stand-alone resource return `201 Created` — registering a restaurant, registering a rider, registering a customer, creating a menu item, placing an order, opening a return, opening a work order, and dispatching (which creates a fresh `Assignment`). """More self-tests — covering boundary cases and remaining PRD rules."""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import sys

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
ROOT = os.path.dirname(HERE)
sys.path.insert(0, ROOT)

from tests.harness import TestClient, TestRunner

NYC = (40.7128, -74.0060)
NEAR_NYC = (40.7129, -74.0061)
FAR_NYC = (40.7228, -74.0060)
VERY_FAR_NYC = (41.0000, -73.5000)  # ~62km away — high fee bands

CLIENT = TestClient()
R = TestRunner()


# --- helpers (same as run_tests_extra) ---
def register_active_restaurant(name="R", coords=NYC, commission_override=None):
    s, b = CLIENT.request("POST", "/api/restaurants", role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="admin",
                          body={"name": name, "address": "1 a", "lat": coords[0], "lng": coords[1],
                                "commission_rate_override": commission_override})
    rid = b["data"]["id"]
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/restaurants/{rid}/approve",
                   role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="admin")
    return b["data"]


def register_customer(phone="555", coords=NEAR_NYC):
    s, b = CLIENT.request("POST", "/api/customers", role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="admin",
                          body={"name": "C", "phone": phone, "address": "x",
                                "lat": coords[0], "lng": coords[1]})
    return b["data"]


def register_rider(phone="r"):
    s, b = CLIENT.request("POST", "/api/riders", role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="admin",
                          body={"name": "R", "phone": phone})
    return b["data"]


def online(rider):
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/riders/{rider['id']}/go-online",
                   role="Rider", user_id=rider["id"])


def add_menu(rid, price=2000, name="X"):
    s, b = CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/restaurants/{rid}/menu-items",
                          role="Restaurant", user_id=rid,
                          body={"name": name, "price_cents": price})
    return b["data"]


def place_order(cid, rid, items):
    s, b = CLIENT.request("POST", "/api/orders", role="Customer", user_id=cid,
                          body={"customer_id": cid, "restaurant_id": rid, "items": items})
    return b["data"]


def advance(s):
    CLIENT.request("POST", "/api/_clock/advance", role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="admin",
                   body={"seconds": s})


def full_deliver(customer, restaurant, rider, price=2000, qty=1, late_seconds=0):
    m = add_menu(restaurant["id"], price=price)
    o = place_order(customer["id"], restaurant["id"], [{"menu_item_id": m["id"], "quantity": qty}])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/accept",
                   role="Restaurant", user_id=restaurant["id"])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/start-preparing",
                   role="Restaurant", user_id=restaurant["id"])
    from store import STORE
    aid = next(a["id"] for a in STORE.assignments.values()
                if a["order_id"] == o["id"] and a["status"] == "OFFERED")
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/assignments/{aid}/accept", role="Rider", user_id=rider["id"])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/ready",
                   role="Restaurant", user_id=restaurant["id"])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/assignments/{aid}/pickup", role="Rider", user_id=rider["id"])
    if late_seconds:
        advance(45 * 60 + late_seconds)
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/assignments/{aid}/deliver", role="Rider", user_id=rider["id"])
    return o, aid


# === Late delivery boundaries ===

def t_credit_balance_unaffected_by_placement_and_cancel():
    CLIENT.reset()
    r = register_active_restaurant(); c = register_customer()
    # Manually set credit to nonzero
    from store import STORE
    STORE.customers[c["id"]]["credit_balance_cents"] = 1000
    m = add_menu(r["id"])
    o = place_order(c["id"], r["id"], [{"menu_item_id": m["id"], "quantity": 1}])
    s, cb = CLIENT.request("GET", f"/api/customers/{c['id']}",
                           role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="admin")
    # PRD §3.5 says credit_balance_cents is not affected on cancellation.
    # We don't decrement it on placement either — leave it alone unless PRD-specified mutations occur.
    s, _ = CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/cancel",
                          role="Customer", user_id=c["id"])
    s, cb2 = CLIENT.request("GET", f"/api/customers/{c['id']}",
                            role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="admin")
    assert cb2["data"]["credit_balance_cents"] == 1000


TESTS = [
    ("late exactly 1 min fine 200", t_late_exactly_1),

"""Final self-tests — covering remaining PRD branches (dispatch selection,
WO closure, override boundaries, fine query scopes, list filters, etc.)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import sys

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
ROOT = os.path.dirname(HERE)
sys.path.insert(0, ROOT)

from tests.harness import TestClient, TestRunner

NYC = (40.7128, -74.0060)
NEAR_NYC = (40.7129, -74.0061)

CLIENT = TestClient()
R = TestRunner()


def make_restaurant(name="R", coords=NYC, override=None):
    s, b = CLIENT.request("POST", "/api/restaurants", role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="admin",
                          body={"name": name, "address": "1 a", "lat": coords[0], "lng": coords[1],
                                "commission_rate_override": override})
    rid = b["data"]["id"]
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/restaurants/{rid}/approve",
                   role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="admin")
    return b["data"]


def make_customer(phone="555", coords=NEAR_NYC):
    s, b = CLIENT.request("POST", "/api/customers", role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="admin",
                          body={"name": "C", "phone": phone, "address": "x",
                                "lat": coords[0], "lng": coords[1]})
    return b["data"]


def make_rider(phone="r"):
    s, b = CLIENT.request("POST", "/api/riders", role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="admin",
                          body={"name": "R", "phone": phone})
    return b["data"]


def go_online(r):
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/riders/{r['id']}/go-online", role="Rider", user_id=r["id"])


def add_menu(rid, price=2000, name="X"):
    s, b = CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/restaurants/{rid}/menu-items",
                          role="Restaurant", user_id=rid,
                          body={"name": name, "price_cents": price})
    return b["data"]


def place_order(cid, rid, items):
    s, b = CLIENT.request("POST", "/api/orders", role="Customer", user_id=cid,
                          body={"customer_id": cid, "restaurant_id": rid, "items": items})
    return b["data"]


# === Restaurant override boundary values ===
def t_override_boundary_low():
    CLIENT.reset()
    # 0.05 lower bound — accepted
    s, b = CLIENT.request("POST", "/api/restaurants", role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="admin",
                          body={"name": "Q", "address": "x", "lat": 40.0, "lng": -74.0,
                                "commission_rate_override": 0.05})
    assert s == 201, (s, b)


def t_override_boundary_high():
    CLIENT.reset()
    s, b = CLIENT.request("POST", "/api/restaurants", role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="admin",
                          body={"name": "Q", "address": "x", "lat": 40.0, "lng": -74.0,
                                "commission_rate_override": 0.35})
    assert s == 201, (s, b)


def t_override_outside_range():
    CLIENT.reset()
    s, b = CLIENT.request("POST", "/api/restaurants", role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="admin",
                          body={"name": "Q", "address": "x", "lat": 40.0, "lng": -74.0,
                                "commission_rate_override": 0.04})
    assert s == 422, (s, b)
    s, b = CLIENT.request("POST", "/api/restaurants", role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="admin",
                          body={"name": "Q2", "address": "x", "lat": 40.0, "lng": -74.0,
                                "commission_rate_override": 0.36})
    assert s == 422, (s, b)


# === Dispatch: candidate excludes rider holding a live assignment for same order ===
def t_dispatch_excludes_existing_rider():
    """When a rider rejects, re-dispatch must go to a different rider — same rider should be excluded."""
    CLIENT.reset()
    r = make_restaurant()
    c = make_customer()
    rider1 = make_rider("r1"); go_online(rider1)
    m = add_menu(r["id"])
    o = place_order(c["id"], r["id"], [{"menu_item_id": m["id"], "quantity": 1}])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/accept", role="Restaurant", user_id=r["id"])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/start-preparing", role="Restaurant", user_id=r["id"])
    from store import STORE
    a1 = next(a for a in STORE.assignments.values() if a["order_id"] == o["id"] and a["status"] == "OFFERED")
    # Reject — no other rider available, so redispatch finds empty pool, no fresh OFFERED created.
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/assignments/{a1['id']}/reject", role="Rider", user_id=rider1["id"])
    # The original assignment is REJECTED, no new live one should exist for rider1.
    live = [a for a in STORE.assignments.values()
            if a["order_id"] == o["id"] and a["status"] == "OFFERED"]
    # Pool was empty (rider1 just rejected so they're excluded — no other riders).
    assert live == [], live


def t_dispatch_pool_empty_returns_invalid_state():
    """Manual /dispatch when there are no riders → ERR_INVALID_STATE."""
    CLIENT.reset()
    r = make_restaurant(); c = make_customer()
    m = add_menu(r["id"])
    o = place_order(c["id"], r["id"], [{"menu_item_id": m["id"], "quantity": 1}])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/accept", role="Restaurant", user_id=r["id"])
    s, b = CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/dispatch",
                          role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="admin")
    assert s == 409 and b["data"]["error_id"] == "ERR_INVALID_STATE", (s, b)


def t_dispatch_tiebreaker_created_at_desc():
    """Among AVAILABLE riders, most recently registered wins."""
    CLIENT.reset()
    r = make_restaurant(); c = make_customer()
    r1 = make_rider("r1"); go_online(r1)
    r2 = make_rider("r2"); go_online(r2)
    r3 = make_rider("r3"); go_online(r3)  # registered last
    m = add_menu(r["id"])
    o = place_order(c["id"], r["id"], [{"menu_item_id": m["id"], "quantity": 1}])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/accept", role="Restaurant", user_id=r["id"])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/start-preparing", role="Restaurant", user_id=r["id"])
    from store import STORE
    live = next(a for a in STORE.assignments.values() if a["order_id"] == o["id"] and a["status"] == "OFFERED")
    assert live["rider_id"] == r3["id"], (live, r3, r2, r1)


# === Order list filter by rider_id ===
def t_orders_list_by_rider():
    CLIENT.reset()
    r = make_restaurant(); c = make_customer()
    rider = make_rider(); go_online(rider)
    m = add_menu(r["id"])
    o = place_order(c["id"], r["id"], [{"menu_item_id": m["id"], "quantity": 1}])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/accept", role="Restaurant", user_id=r["id"])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/start-preparing", role="Restaurant", user_id=r["id"])
    from store import STORE
    a = next(a for a in STORE.assignments.values() if a["order_id"] == o["id"])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/assignments/{a['id']}/accept", role="Rider", user_id=rider["id"])
    s, b = CLIENT.request("GET", f"/api/orders?rider_id={rider['id']}",
                          role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="admin")
    assert s == 200
    ids = [r["id"] for r in b["data"]]
    assert o["id"] in ids


# === menu_item_id from different restaurant → ERR_RESTAURANT_UNAVAILABLE ===
def t_menu_item_from_different_restaurant():
    CLIENT.reset()
    r1 = make_restaurant("R1"); r2 = make_restaurant("R2", coords=(40.8, -74.1))
    c = make_customer()
    m_at_r2 = add_menu(r2["id"])
    s, b = CLIENT.request("POST", "/api/orders", role="Customer", user_id=c["id"],
                          body={"customer_id": c["id"], "restaurant_id": r1["id"],
                                "items": [{"menu_item_id": m_at_r2["id"], "quantity": 1}]})
    assert s == 422 and b["data"]["error_id"] == "ERR_RESTAURANT_UNAVAILABLE", (s, b)


# === Customer ABUSIVE_RETURN deducts credit_balance via fine ===
def t_abusive_fine_deducts_credit():
    CLIENT.reset()
    r = make_restaurant(); c = make_customer()
    rider = make_rider(); go_online(rider)
    from store import STORE
    STORE.customers[c["id"]]["trust_score"] = 0.2
    STORE.customers[c["id"]]["credit_balance_cents"] = 10000
    # Run a delivery
    m = add_menu(r["id"], price=3000)
    o = place_order(c["id"], r["id"], [{"menu_item_id": m["id"], "quantity": 1}])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/accept", role="Restaurant", user_id=r["id"])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/start-preparing", role="Restaurant", user_id=r["id"])
    a = next(a for a in STORE.assignments.values() if a["order_id"] == o["id"])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/assignments/{a['id']}/accept", role="Rider", user_id=rider["id"])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/ready", role="Restaurant", user_id=r["id"])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/assignments/{a['id']}/pickup", role="Rider", user_id=rider["id"])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/assignments/{a['id']}/deliver", role="Rider", user_id=rider["id"])
    credit_before = STORE.customers[c["id"]]["credit_balance_cents"]
    # Open + approve return with reason QUALITY_ISSUE — abusive fine = approved cents
    s, ret = CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/returns",
                            role="Customer", user_id=c["id"],
                            body={"reason": "QUALITY_ISSUE", "requested_refund_cents": 1000})
    assert s == 201, (s, ret)
    # Approval credits 1000, then ABUSIVE_RETURN fine of 1000 deducts 1000 from credit.
    s, ap = CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/returns/{ret['data']['id']}/approve",
                           role="CustomerService", user_id="cs",
                           body={"approved_refund_cents": 1000})
    assert s == 200, (s, ap)
    credit_after = STORE.customers[c["id"]]["credit_balance_cents"]
    # +1000 from approve, -1000 from abusive fine → net 0
    assert credit_after == credit_before, (credit_before, credit_after)


# === WorkOrder close only from RESOLVED ===
def t_wo_close_only_from_resolved():
    CLIENT.reset()
    c = make_customer()
    s, b = CLIENT.request("POST", "/api/work-orders", role="Customer", user_id=c["id"],
                          body={"opened_by_role": "CUSTOMER", "opened_by_id": c["id"],
                                "category": "OTHER"})
    wid = b["data"]["id"]
    # Try close while OPEN
    s, b = CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/work-orders/{wid}/close",
                          role="CustomerService", user_id="cs")
    assert s == 409 and b["data"]["error_id"] == "ERR_INVALID_STATE", (s, b)


# === Fine query scope for Customer ===
def t_fine_query_scope_customer():
    CLIENT.reset()
    r = make_restaurant(); c = make_customer(); c2 = make_customer(phone="999")
    from store import STORE
    STORE.customers[c["id"]]["trust_score"] = 0.0
    rider = make_rider(); go_online(rider)
    # Deliver, then return → abusive fine on c
    m = add_menu(r["id"], price=3000)
    o = place_order(c["id"], r["id"], [{"menu_item_id": m["id"], "quantity": 1}])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/accept", role="Restaurant", user_id=r["id"])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/start-preparing", role="Restaurant", user_id=r["id"])
    a = next(a for a in STORE.assignments.values() if a["order_id"] == o["id"])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/assignments/{a['id']}/accept", role="Rider", user_id=rider["id"])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/ready", role="Restaurant", user_id=r["id"])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/assignments/{a['id']}/pickup", role="Rider", user_id=rider["id"])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/assignments/{a['id']}/deliver", role="Rider", user_id=rider["id"])
    s, ret = CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/returns",
                            role="Customer", user_id=c["id"],
                            body={"reason": "QUALITY_ISSUE", "requested_refund_cents": 500})
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/returns/{ret['data']['id']}/approve",
                   role="CustomerService", user_id="cs",
                   body={"approved_refund_cents": 500})
    # Customer c queries their own fines — should work.
    s, b = CLIENT.request("GET", f"/api/fines?subject_type=CUSTOMER&subject_id={c['id']}",
                          role="Customer", user_id=c["id"])
    assert s == 200 and len(b["data"]) >= 1, (s, b)
    # Customer c2 querying c's fines — FORBIDDEN.
    s, b = CLIENT.request("GET", f"/api/fines?subject_type=CUSTOMER&subject_id={c['id']}",
                          role="Customer", user_id=c2["id"])
    assert s == 403, (s, b)
    # PlatformAdmin can query any.
    s, b = CLIENT.request("GET", f"/api/fines?subject_type=CUSTOMER&subject_id={c['id']}",
                          role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="admin")
    assert s == 200, (s, b)


# === Fines query for Restaurant scope ===
def t_fine_query_restaurant_only_own():
    CLIENT.reset()
    r = make_restaurant(); r2 = make_restaurant("R2", coords=(40.8, -74.1))
    s, b = CLIENT.request("GET", f"/api/fines?subject_type=RESTAURANT&subject_id={r2['id']}",
                          role="Restaurant", user_id=r["id"])
    assert s == 403, (s, b)


# === Fine read RBAC ===
def t_fine_read_scope():
    CLIENT.reset()
    r = make_restaurant(); c = make_customer()
    rider = make_rider(); go_online(rider)
    from store import STORE
    m = add_menu(r["id"], price=2000)
    o = place_order(c["id"], r["id"], [{"menu_item_id": m["id"], "quantity": 1}])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/accept", role="Restaurant", user_id=r["id"])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/start-preparing", role="Restaurant", user_id=r["id"])
    a = next(a for a in STORE.assignments.values() if a["order_id"] == o["id"])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/assignments/{a['id']}/accept", role="Rider", user_id=rider["id"])
    # Rider cancels → NO_SHOW fine on rider
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/assignments/{a['id']}/cancel", role="Rider", user_id=rider["id"])
    fine = next(f for f in STORE.fines.values() if f["subject_id"] == rider["id"])
    # Rider can read own
    s, b = CLIENT.request("GET", f"/api/fines/{fine['id']}", role="Rider", user_id=rider["id"])
    assert s == 200, (s, b)
    # Another rider can't
    rider2 = make_rider("rr2"); go_online(rider2)
    s, b = CLIENT.request("GET", f"/api/fines/{fine['id']}", role="Rider", user_id=rider2["id"])
    assert s == 403, (s, b)


# === Menu-item update only by owner / admin ===
def t_menu_item_patch_ownership():
    CLIENT.reset()
    r = make_restaurant(); r2 = make_restaurant("R2", coords=(40.8, -74.1))
    m = add_menu(r["id"])
    # Another restaurant can't patch
    s, b = CLIENT.request("PATCH", f"/api/menu-items/{m['id']}",
                          role="Restaurant", user_id=r2["id"],
                          body={"price_cents": 1500})
    assert s == 403, (s, b)
    # Owner can
    s, b = CLIENT.request("PATCH", f"/api/menu-items/{m['id']}",
                          role="Restaurant", user_id=r["id"],
                          body={"price_cents": 1500})
    assert s == 200, (s, b)


# === Menu item price boundary ===
def t_menu_item_price_boundary():
    CLIENT.reset()
    r = make_restaurant()
    # 0 → invalid
    s, b = CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/restaurants/{r['id']}/menu-items",
                          role="Restaurant", user_id=r["id"],
                          body={"name": "x", "price_cents": 0})
    assert s == 422, (s, b)
    # 1_000_001 → invalid
    s, b = CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/restaurants/{r['id']}/menu-items",
                          role="Restaurant", user_id=r["id"],
                          body={"name": "x", "price_cents": 1_000_001})
    assert s == 422, (s, b)
    # 1 → ok
    s, b = CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/restaurants/{r['id']}/menu-items",
                          role="Restaurant", user_id=r["id"],
                          body={"name": "x", "price_cents": 1})
    assert s == 201, (s, b)


# === Restaurant reinstate ===
def t_restaurant_reinstate():
    CLIENT.reset()
    r = make_restaurant()
    rider = make_rider(); go_online(rider)
    # Force suspension by manipulating rider metrics? No — restaurant suspend works without preconditions.
    s, b = CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/restaurants/{r['id']}/suspend",
                          role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="admin")
    assert s == 200 and b["data"]["status"] == "SUSPENDED"
    s, b = CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/restaurants/{r['id']}/reinstate",
                          role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="admin")
    assert s == 200 and b["data"]["status"] == "ACTIVE"
    # Reinstate from PENDING_APPROVAL should fail
    s, b = CLIENT.request("POST", "/api/restaurants", role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="admin",
                          body={"name": "Q", "address": "x", "lat": 40.0, "lng": -74.0})
    rid = b["data"]["id"]
    s, b = CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/restaurants/{rid}/reinstate",
                          role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="admin")
    assert s == 409, (s, b)


# === Distance rounding 1 decimal ===
def t_distance_rounded_to_one_decimal():
    """A 1.05 km distance should round to 1.1 → 2 bands (ceil(1.1) = 2)."""
    CLIENT.reset()
    # Use lat differences such that distance ≈ 1.05 km
    r = make_restaurant("R", coords=(40.0, -74.0))
    # 0.00945° lat ≈ 1.052 km
    c = make_customer(coords=(40.00945, -74.0))
    m = add_menu(r["id"])
    o = place_order(c["id"], r["id"], [{"menu_item_id": m["id"], "quantity": 1}])
    # distance_km should round to 1.1
    assert o["distance_km"] == 1.1, o["distance_km"]
    # Off-peak provisional fee: 300 + 120*ceil(1.1) = 300 + 240 = 540
    # But this depends on whether it's peak — let's just assert the formula
    expected_bands = 2
    expected_fee = 300 + 120 * expected_bands + (200 if o["is_peak"] else 0)
    assert o["provisional_delivery_fee_cents"] == expected_fee, (o,)


# === Restaurant CLOSED is terminal ===
def t_restaurant_cannot_close_via_endpoint():
    """PRD: CLOSED is a terminal lifecycle bucket but no endpoint sets it.
    Just confirm reinstate from CLOSED isn't possible (can't reach CLOSED via API)."""
    CLIENT.reset()
    r = make_restaurant()
    # No /close endpoint exists in the API surface — this is fine.
    s, b = CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/restaurants/{r['id']}/close",
                          role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="admin")
    assert s == 404, (s, b)  # endpoint doesn't exist


# === Bonus tier exact boundary scores ===
def t_bonus_tier_exact_900_is_platinum():
    from bonus import compute_bonus_tier
    # 0.6*on + 0.3*acc + 0.1*(rating/5) — pick values that score exactly 0.900
    # on=1, acc=1, rating=0 → 0.6 + 0.3 + 0 = 0.9
    assert compute_bonus_tier(1.0, 1.0, 0.0) == "PLATINUM"
    # 0.6*on + 0.3*acc + 0.1*(rating/5) = 0.8 → on=1, acc=0.667, rating=0
    # Actually use: on=0.5, acc=1.0, rating=5.0 → 0.3+0.3+0.1 = 0.7 → SILVER
    assert compute_bonus_tier(0.5, 1.0, 5.0) == "SILVER"
    # 0.0 → BRONZE
    assert compute_bonus_tier(0.0, 0.0, 0.0) == "BRONZE"


# === payment_status FULLY_REFUNDED when approved == subtotal ===
def t_fully_refunded_status():
    CLIENT.reset()
    r = make_restaurant(); c = make_customer()
    rider = make_rider(); go_online(rider)
    from store import STORE
    m = add_menu(r["id"], price=3000)
    o = place_order(c["id"], r["id"], [{"menu_item_id": m["id"], "quantity": 1}])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/accept", role="Restaurant", user_id=r["id"])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/start-preparing", role="Restaurant", user_id=r["id"])
    a = next(a for a in STORE.assignments.values() if a["order_id"] == o["id"])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/assignments/{a['id']}/accept", role="Rider", user_id=rider["id"])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/ready", role="Restaurant", user_id=r["id"])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/assignments/{a['id']}/pickup", role="Rider", user_id=rider["id"])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/assignments/{a['id']}/deliver", role="Rider", user_id=rider["id"])
    s, ret = CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/returns",
                            role="Customer", user_id=c["id"],
                            body={"reason": "WRONG_ITEM", "requested_refund_cents": 3000})
    s, ap = CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/returns/{ret['data']['id']}/approve",
                           role="CustomerService", user_id="cs",
                           body={"approved_refund_cents": 3000})
    s, ob = CLIENT.request("GET", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}", role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="admin")
    assert ob["data"]["payment_status"] == "FULLY_REFUNDED", ob["data"]


# === order with quantity > 1 computes subtotal correctly ===
def t_subtotal_quantity_aware():
    CLIENT.reset()
    r = make_restaurant(); c = make_customer()
    m = add_menu(r["id"], price=500)
    o = place_order(c["id"], r["id"], [{"menu_item_id": m["id"], "quantity": 4}])
    assert o["subtotal_cents"] == 2000, o


# === Assignment record has no version/updated_at ===
def t_assignment_no_version_field():
    CLIENT.reset()
    r = make_restaurant(); c = make_customer()
    rider = make_rider(); go_online(rider)
    from store import STORE
    m = add_menu(r["id"])
    o = place_order(c["id"], r["id"], [{"menu_item_id": m["id"], "quantity": 1}])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/accept", role="Restaurant", user_id=r["id"])

# === Fine record has no version/updated_at ===
def t_fine_no_version_field():
    CLIENT.reset()

    m = add_menu(r["id"])

    fine = next(f for f in STORE.fines.values() if f["reason"] == "RIDER_NO_SHOW")
    s, b = CLIENT.request("GET", f"/api/fines/{fine['id']}",
                          role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="admin")
    assert "version" not in b["data"]
    assert "updated_at" not in b["data"]


# === Suspended restaurant cancels PLACED orders with payment_status VOIDED ===
def t_suspend_cancels_with_voided_payment():
    CLIENT.reset()
    r = make_restaurant(); c = make_customer()
    m = add_menu(r["id"])

# === Empty pool dispatch from start-preparing → no offer ===
def t_start_preparing_no_riders_no_offer():
    CLIENT.reset()
    r = make_restaurant(); c = make_customer()
    m = add_menu(r["id"])
    o = place_order(c["id"], r["id"], [{"menu_item_id": m["id"], "quantity": 1}])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/accept", role="Restaurant", user_id=r["id"])
    s, b = CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/start-preparing",
                          role="Restaurant", user_id=r["id"])
    # PRD §3.5: start-preparing advances order, also opens dispatch but no error if pool empty.
    assert s == 200
    from store import STORE
    assert STORE.orders[o["id"]]["status"] == "PREPARING"
    live = [a for a in STORE.assignments.values()
            if a["order_id"] == o["id"] and a["status"] == "OFFERED"]
    assert live == []


# === Auth empty string ===
def t_auth_empty_user_id():
    CLIENT.reset()
    # X-User-ID empty → still treated as present?
    s, b = CLIENT.request("GET", "/api/restaurants", role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="")
    # PRD §2.1: missing header → ERR_AUTH_REQUIRED. Empty string is debatable but treated as missing.
    assert s == 401, (s, b)


# === ERR_VALIDATION for malformed body ===
def t_generic_validation_error():
    CLIENT.reset()
    s, b = CLIENT.request("POST", "/api/restaurants", role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="admin",
                          body={"name": ""})  # missing address, empty name
    assert s == 422 and b["data"]["error_id"] in ("ERR_VALIDATION",), (s, b)


# === Customer can read own work order, not others ===
def t_wo_read_scope():
    CLIENT.reset()
    c = make_customer(); c2 = make_customer(phone="999")
    s, b = CLIENT.request("POST", "/api/work-orders",
                          role="Customer", user_id=c["id"],

                                "category": "OTHER"})
    wid = b["data"]["id"]
    s, b = CLIENT.request("GET", f"/api/work-orders/{wid}", role="Customer", user_id=c["id"])
    assert s == 200
    s, b = CLIENT.request("GET", f"/api/work-orders/{wid}", role="Customer", user_id=c2["id"])
    assert s == 403, (s, b)


TESTS = [
    ("override boundary low 0.05", t_override_boundary_low),
    ("override boundary high 0.35", t_override_boundary_high),
    ("override outside range rejected", t_override_outside_range),
    ("dispatch excludes rider with existing assignment", t_dispatch_excludes_existing_rider),
    ("dispatch pool empty → INVALID_STATE", t_dispatch_pool_empty_returns_invalid_state),
    ("dispatch tie-breaker: most recent rider wins", t_dispatch_tiebreaker_created_at_desc),
    ("orders list filter by rider_id", t_orders_list_by_rider),
    ("menu_item from different restaurant → UNAVAILABLE", t_menu_item_from_different_restaurant),
    ("abusive fine deducts credit balance", t_abusive_fine_deducts_credit),
    ("WO close only from RESOLVED", t_wo_close_only_from_resolved),
    ("fine query — customer scope", t_fine_query_scope_customer),
    ("fine query — restaurant only own", t_fine_query_restaurant_only_own),
    ("fine read RBAC", t_fine_read_scope),
    ("menu item patch ownership", t_menu_item_patch_ownership),
    ("menu item price boundary", t_menu_item_price_boundary),
    ("restaurant reinstate from SUSPENDED", t_restaurant_reinstate),
    ("distance rounded to 1 decimal", t_distance_rounded_to_one_decimal),
    ("restaurant has no /close endpoint", t_restaurant_cannot_close_via_endpoint),
    ("bonus tier 0.900 = PLATINUM exact", t_bonus_tier_exact_900_is_platinum),
    ("FULLY_REFUNDED status on full refund", t_fully_refunded_status),
    ("subtotal quantity aware", t_subtotal_quantity_aware),
    ("assignment has no version/updated_at", t_assignment_no_version_field),
    ("fine has no version/updated_at", t_fine_no_version_field),
    ("suspend cancels PLACED with VOIDED payment", t_suspend_cancels_with_voided_payment),
    ("orders list filter by status", t_orders_list_status_filter),
    ("start-preparing with no riders → no offer, order still PREPARING", t_start_preparing_no_riders_no_offer),
    ("auth — empty user id → 401", t_auth_empty_user_id),
    ("generic ERR_VALIDATION for malformed body", t_generic_validation_error),
    ("WO read scope — only opener", t_wo_read_scope),
]

if __name__ == "__main__":
    for name, fn in TESTS:
        R.run(name, fn)
    ok = R.report()
    sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)

"""Final self-tests — covering remaining PRD branches (dispatch selection,
WO closure, override boundaries, fine query scopes, list filters, etc.)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import sys

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
ROOT = os.path.dirname(HERE)
sys.path.insert(0, ROOT)

from tests.harness import TestClient, TestRunner

NYC = (40.7128, -74.0060)
NEAR_NYC = (40.7129, -74.0061)

CLIENT = TestClient()
R = TestRunner()


def make_restaurant(name="R", coords=NYC, override=None):
    s, b = CLIENT.request("POST", "/api/restaurants", role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="admin",
                          body={"name": name, "address": "1 a", "lat": coords[0], "lng": coords[1],
                                "commission_rate_override": override})
    rid = b["data"]["id"]
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/restaurants/{rid}/approve",
                   role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="admin")
    return b["data"]


def make_customer(phone="555", coords=NEAR_NYC):
    s, b = CLIENT.request("POST", "/api/customers", role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="admin",
                          body={"name": "C", "phone": phone, "address": "x",
                                "lat": coords[0], "lng": coords[1]})
    return b["data"]


def make_rider(phone="r"):
    s, b = CLIENT.request("POST", "/api/riders", role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="admin",
                          body={"name": "R", "phone": phone})
    return b["data"]


def go_online(r):
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/riders/{r['id']}/go-online", role="Rider", user_id=r["id"])


def add_menu(rid, price=2000, name="X"):
    s, b = CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/restaurants/{rid}/menu-items",
                          role="Restaurant", user_id=rid,
                          body={"name": name, "price_cents": price})
    return b["data"]


def place_order(cid, rid, items):
    s, b = CLIENT.request("POST", "/api/orders", role="Customer", user_id=cid,
                          body={"customer_id": cid, "restaurant_id": rid, "items": items})
    return b["data"]


# === Restaurant override boundary values ===
def t_override_boundary_low():
    CLIENT.reset()
    # 0.05 lower bound — accepted
    s, b = CLIENT.request("POST", "/api/restaurants", role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="admin",
                          body={"name": "Q", "address": "x", "lat": 40.0, "lng": -74.0,
                                "commission_rate_override": 0.05})
    assert s == 201, (s, b)


def t_override_boundary_high():
    CLIENT.reset()
    s, b = CLIENT.request("POST", "/api/restaurants", role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="admin",
                          body={"name": "Q", "address": "x", "lat": 40.0, "lng": -74.0,
                                "commission_rate_override": 0.35})
    assert s == 201, (s, b)


def t_override_outside_range():
    CLIENT.reset()
    s, b = CLIENT.request("POST", "/api/restaurants", role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="admin",
                          body={"name": "Q", "address": "x", "lat": 40.0, "lng": -74.0,
                                "commission_rate_override": 0.04})
    assert s == 422, (s, b)
    s, b = CLIENT.request("POST", "/api/restaurants", role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="admin",
                          body={"name": "Q2", "address": "x", "lat": 40.0, "lng": -74.0,
                                "commission_rate_override": 0.36})
    assert s == 422, (s, b)


# === Dispatch: candidate excludes rider holding a live assignment for same order ===
def t_dispatch_excludes_existing_rider():
    """When a rider rejects, re-dispatch must go to a different rider — same rider should be excluded."""
    CLIENT.reset()
    r = make_restaurant()
    c = make_customer()
    rider1 = make_rider("r1"); go_online(rider1)
    m = add_menu(r["id"])
    o = place_order(c["id"], r["id"], [{"menu_item_id": m["id"], "quantity": 1}])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/accept", role="Restaurant", user_id=r["id"])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/start-preparing", role="Restaurant", user_id=r["id"])
    from store import STORE
    a1 = next(a for a in STORE.assignments.values() if a["order_id"] == o["id"] and a["status"] == "OFFERED")
    # Reject — no other rider available, so redispatch finds empty pool, no fresh OFFERED created.
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/assignments/{a1['id']}/reject", role="Rider", user_id=rider1["id"])
    # The original assignment is REJECTED, no new live one should exist for rider1.
    live = [a for a in STORE.assignments.values()
            if a["order_id"] == o["id"] and a["status"] == "OFFERED"]
    # Pool was empty (rider1 just rejected so they're excluded — no other riders).
    assert live == [], live


def t_dispatch_pool_empty_returns_invalid_state():
    """Manual /dispatch when there are no riders → ERR_INVALID_STATE."""
    CLIENT.reset()

    m = add_menu(r["id"])

    assert s == 409 and b["data"]["error_id"] == "ERR_INVALID_STATE", (s, b)


def t_dispatch_tiebreaker_created_at_desc():
    """Among AVAILABLE riders, most recently registered wins."""
    CLIENT.reset()
    r = make_restaurant(); c = make_customer()
    r1 = make_rider("r1"); go_online(r1)
    r2 = make_rider("r2"); go_online(r2)
    r3 = make_rider("r3"); go_online(r3)  # registered last
    m = add_menu(r["id"])
    o = place_order(c["id"], r["id"], [{"menu_item_id": m["id"], "quantity": 1}])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/accept", role="Restaurant", user_id=r["id"])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/start-preparing", role="Restaurant", user_id=r["id"])
    from store import STORE
    live = next(a for a in STORE.assignments.values() if a["order_id"] == o["id"] and a["status"] == "OFFERED")
    assert live["rider_id"] == r3["id"], (live, r3, r2, r1)


# === Order list filter by rider_id ===
def t_orders_list_by_rider():
    CLIENT.reset()
    r = make_restaurant(); c = make_customer()
    rider = make_rider(); go_online(rider)
    m = add_menu(r["id"])
    o = place_order(c["id"], r["id"], [{"menu_item_id": m["id"], "quantity": 1}])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/accept", role="Restaurant", user_id=r["id"])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/start-preparing", role="Restaurant", user_id=r["id"])
    from store import STORE
    a = next(a for a in STORE.assignments.values() if a["order_id"] == o["id"])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/assignments/{a['id']}/accept", role="Rider", user_id=rider["id"])
    s, b = CLIENT.request("GET", f"/api/orders?rider_id={rider['id']}",
                          role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="admin")
    assert s == 200
    ids = [r["id"] for r in b["data"]]
    assert o["id"] in ids


# === menu_item_id from different restaurant → ERR_RESTAURANT_UNAVAILABLE ===
def t_menu_item_from_different_restaurant():
    CLIENT.reset()
    r1 = make_restaurant("R1"); r2 = make_restaurant("R2", coords=(40.8, -74.1))
    c = make_customer()
    m_at_r2 = add_menu(r2["id"])
    s, b = CLIENT.request("POST", "/api/orders", role="Customer", user_id=c["id"],
                          body={"customer_id": c["id"], "restaurant_id": r1["id"],

    assert s == 422 and b["data"]["error_id"] == "ERR_RESTAURANT_UNAVAILABLE", (s, b)


# === Customer ABUSIVE_RETURN deducts credit_balance via fine ===
def t_abusive_fine_deducts_credit():
    CLIENT.reset()
    r = make_restaurant(); c = make_customer()
    rider = make_rider(); go_online(rider)
    from store import STORE
    STORE.customers[c["id"]]["trust_score"] = 0.2
    STORE.customers[c["id"]]["credit_balance_cents"] = 10000
    # Run a delivery
    m = add_menu(r["id"], price=3000)
    o = place_order(c["id"], r["id"], [{"menu_item_id": m["id"], "quantity": 1}])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/accept", role="Restaurant", user_id=r["id"])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/start-preparing", role="Restaurant", user_id=r["id"])
    a = next(a for a in STORE.assignments.values() if a["order_id"] == o["id"])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/assignments/{a['id']}/accept", role="Rider", user_id=rider["id"])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/ready", role="Restaurant", user_id=r["id"])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/assignments/{a['id']}/pickup", role="Rider", user_id=rider["id"])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/assignments/{a['id']}/deliver", role="Rider", user_id=rider["id"])
    credit_before = STORE.customers[c["id"]]["credit_balance_cents"]
    # Open + approve return with reason QUALITY_ISSUE — abusive fine = approved cents
    s, ret = CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/returns",
                            role="Customer", user_id=c["id"],
                            body={"reason": "QUALITY_ISSUE", "requested_refund_cents": 1000})
    assert s == 201, (s, ret)
    # Approval credits 1000, then ABUSIVE_RETURN fine of 1000 deducts 1000 from credit.
    s, ap = CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/returns/{ret['data']['id']}/approve",
                           role="CustomerService", user_id="cs",
                           body={"approved_refund_cents": 1000})
    assert s == 200, (s, ap)
    credit_after = STORE.customers[c["id"]]["credit_balance_cents"]
    # +1000 from approve, -1000 from abusive fine → net 0
    assert credit_after == credit_before, (credit_before, credit_after)


# === WorkOrder close only from RESOLVED ===
def t_wo_close_only_from_resolved():
    CLIENT.reset()
    c = make_customer()
    s, b = CLIENT.request("POST", "/api/work-orders", role="Customer", user_id=c["id"],

                          role="CustomerService", user_id="cs")

def t_fine_query_scope_customer():

    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/start-preparing", role="Restaurant", user_id=r["id"])
    a = next(a for a in STORE.assignments.values() if a["order_id"] == o["id"])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/assignments/{a['id']}/accept", role="Rider", user_id=rider["id"])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/ready", role="Restaurant", user_id=r["id"])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/assignments/{a['id']}/pickup", role="Rider", user_id=rider["id"])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/assignments/{a['id']}/deliver", role="Rider", user_id=rider["id"])

                            body={"reason": "QUALITY_ISSUE", "requested_refund_cents": 500})
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/returns/{ret['data']['id']}/approve",
                   role="CustomerService", user_id="cs",
                   body={"approved_refund_cents": 500})
    # Customer c queries their own fines — should work.
    s, b = CLIENT.request("GET", f"/api/fines?subject_type=CUSTOMER&subject_id={c['id']}",

    s, b = CLIENT.request("GET", f"/api/fines?subject_type=CUSTOMER&subject_id={c['id']}",

    assert s == 403, (s, b)
    # PlatformAdmin can query any.
    s, b = CLIENT.request("GET", f"/api/fines?subject_type=CUSTOMER&subject_id={c['id']}",
                          role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="admin")
    assert s == 200, (s, b)


# === Fines query for Restaurant scope ===
def t_fine_query_restaurant_only_own():
    CLIENT.reset()
    r = make_restaurant(); r2 = make_restaurant("R2", coords=(40.8, -74.1))
    s, b = CLIENT.request("GET", f"/api/fines?subject_type=RESTAURANT&subject_id={r2['id']}",
                          role="Restaurant", user_id=r["id"])
    assert s == 403, (s, b)


# === Fine read RBAC ===
def t_fine_read_scope():
    CLIENT.reset()
    r = make_restaurant(); c = make_customer()
    rider = make_rider(); go_online(rider)
    from store import STORE
    m = add_menu(r["id"], price=2000)
    o = place_order(c["id"], r["id"], [{"menu_item_id": m["id"], "quantity": 1}])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/accept", role="Restaurant", user_id=r["id"])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/start-preparing", role="Restaurant", user_id=r["id"])

    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/assignments/{a['id']}/cancel", role="Rider", user_id=rider["id"])
    fine = next(f for f in STORE.fines.values() if f["subject_id"] == rider["id"])

    s, b = CLIENT.request("GET", f"/api/fines/{fine['id']}", role="Rider", user_id=rider["id"])

# === Menu-item update only by owner / admin ===
def t_menu_item_patch_ownership():
    CLIENT.reset()
    r = make_restaurant(); r2 = make_restaurant("R2", coords=(40.8, -74.1))

    # Owner can
    s, b = CLIENT.request("PATCH", f"/api/menu-items/{m['id']}",
                          role="Restaurant", user_id=r["id"],
                          body={"price_cents": 1500})
    assert s == 200, (s, b)


# === Menu item price boundary ===
def t_menu_item_price_boundary():
    CLIENT.reset()
    r = make_restaurant()
    # 0 → invalid
    s, b = CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/restaurants/{r['id']}/menu-items",

1	"""Dispatch / assignment / route-merging engine. Stubs filled in incrementally."""
2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	from datetime import datetime
6	
7	from clock import CLOCK
8	from errors import APIError
9	from geo import haversine_km
10	from ids import new_id
11	from resources import make_simple, touch
12	from store import STORE
13	
14	
15	def _parse_iso(value: str) -> datetime:
16	    # Accepts "...Z" suffix.
17	    if value.endswith("Z"):
18	        value = value[:-1] + "+00:00"
19	    return datetime.fromisoformat(value)
20	
21	
22	def _is_unpicked(assignment: dict) -> bool:
23	    return assignment["status"] in ("OFFERED", "ACCEPTED")
24	
25	
26	def _restaurant_for(order: dict) -> dict:
27	    return STORE.restaurants[order["restaurant_id"]]
28	
29	
30	def _live_assignment_for_order(order_id: str) -> dict | None:
31	    for a in STORE.assignments.values():
32	        if a["order_id"] == order_id and a["status"] in ("OFFERED", "ACCEPTED", "PICKED_UP"):
33	            return a
34	    return None
35	
36	
37	def _rider_holds_live(rider_id: str, order_id: str) -> bool:
38	    for a in STORE.assignments.values():
39	        if (a["rider_id"] == rider_id and a["order_id"] == order_id
40	                and a["status"] in ("OFFERED", "ACCEPTED", "PICKED_UP")):
41	            return True
42	    return False
43	
44	
45	def _active_route_group_for(rider_id: str) -> dict | None:
46	    for g in STORE.route_groups.values():
47	        if g["rider_id"] == rider_id and g["status"] == "ACTIVE":
48	            return g
49	    return None
50	
51	
52	def _candidate_pool(order: dict) -> list[dict]:
53	    """Pick the best candidate rider per dispatch rules; return ordered list."""
54	    restaurant = _restaurant_for(order)
55	    eligible = []
56	    for rider in STORE.riders.values():
57	        if rider["status"] not in ("AVAILABLE", "ON_DELIVERY"):
58	            continue
59	        if _rider_holds_live(rider["id"], order["id"]):
60	            continue
61	        eligible.append(rider)
62	
63	    def sort_key(rider: dict):
64	        # 0 = preferred (merge-eligible ON_DELIVERY), 1 = otherwise
65	        merge_pref = 1
66	        if rider["status"] == "ON_DELIVERY":
67	            group = _active_route_group_for(rider["id"])
68	            if group is not None:
69	                for aid in group["assignment_ids"]:
70	                    a = STORE.assignments.get(aid)
71	                    if a is None or not _is_unpicked(a):
72	                        continue
73	                    other_order = STORE.orders.get(a["order_id"])
74	                    if other_order is None:
75	                        continue
76	                    other_rest = STORE.restaurants.get(other_order["restaurant_id"])
77	                    if other_rest is None:
78	                        continue
79	                    d_m = haversine_km(restaurant["lat"], restaurant["lng"],
80	                                        other_rest["lat"], other_rest["lng"]) * 1000.0
81	                    if d_m <= 500.0:
82	                        merge_pref = 0
83	                        break
84	        # tie-break: created_at DESC, then id ASC
85	        return (merge_pref, _negate_iso(rider["created_at"]), rider["id"])
86	
87	    eligible.sort(key=sort_key)
88	    return eligible
89	
90	
91	def _negate_iso(ts: str) -> str:
92	    """Return a key that sorts DESC by ts when used in ASC sort context."""
93	    # Invert each char using ord arithmetic: easiest is to use a tuple with negated epoch.
94	    dt = _parse_iso(ts)
95	    return -dt.timestamp()
96	
97	
98	def open_dispatch(order: dict) -> dict | None:
99	    """Create a fresh OFFERED Assignment for order, or return None when no candidates."""
100	    pool = _candidate_pool(order)
101	    if not pool:
102	        return None
103	    rider = pool[0]
104	    now = CLOCK.now_iso()
105	    assignment = make_simple({
106	        "order_id": order["id"],
107	        "rider_id": rider["id"],
108	        "status": "OFFERED",
109	        "offered_at": now,
110	        "accepted_at": None,
111	        "picked_up_at": None,
112	        "delivered_at": None,
113	        "final_delivery_fee_cents": None,
114	        "route_group_id": None,
115	    })
116	    STORE.assignments[assignment["id"]] = assignment
117	    return assignment
118	
119	
120	def force_dispatch(order: dict) -> dict:
121	    """Dispatch a fresh assignment; raise ERR_INVALID_STATE when no candidates."""
122	    assignment = open_dispatch(order)
123	    if assignment is None:
124	        raise APIError("ERR_INVALID_STATE", "No eligible rider available for dispatch.")
125	    return assignment
126	
127	
128	def sweep_offer_timeouts() -> None:
129	    """Move any OFFERED assignment >= 60s old to REJECTED and redispatch."""
130	    now = CLOCK.now()
131	    affected: list[dict] = []
132	    for assignment in list(STORE.assignments.values()):
133	        if assignment["status"] != "OFFERED":
134	            continue
135	        offered = _parse_iso(assignment["offered_at"])
136	        if (now - offered).total_seconds() >= 60.0:
137	            affected.append(assignment)
138	
139	    for assignment in affected:
140	        assignment["status"] = "REJECTED"
141	        # No version on Assignment; just recompute rider acceptance_rate.
142	        rider = STORE.riders.get(assignment["rider_id"])
143	        if rider is not None:
144	            from rider_metrics import recompute_acceptance_rate
145	            recompute_acceptance_rate(rider)
146	            touch(rider)
147	        order = STORE.orders.get(assignment["order_id"])
148	        # Redispatch only when the order still needs a rider.
149	        if order is None:
150	            continue
151	        if order["status"] in ("RESTAURANT_ACCEPTED", "PREPARING", "READY_FOR_PICKUP"):
152	            if _live_assignment_for_order(order["id"]) is None:
153	                open_dispatch(order)

# === Dispatch: explicit /dispatch while one rider holds OFFERED targets a different rider ===
def t_dispatch_excludes_only_live_holders():
    """PRD §3.6: '/dispatch always creates a new OFFERED Assignment so long as the pool is non-empty'.
    The rider currently OFFERED is excluded from the new dispatch's pool."""
    CLIENT.reset()
    r = make_restaurant()
    c = make_customer()
    rider1 = make_rider("r1"); go_online(rider1)
    rider2 = make_rider("r2"); go_online(rider2)
    m = add_menu(r["id"])
    o = place_order(c["id"], r["id"], [{"menu_item_id": m["id"], "quantity": 1}])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/accept", role="Restaurant", user_id=r["id"])
    CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/start-preparing", role="Restaurant", user_id=r["id"])
    from store import STORE
    # First OFFERED should go to rider2 (most recently registered).
    a1 = next(a for a in STORE.assignments.values() if a["order_id"] == o["id"] and a["status"] == "OFFERED")
    first_rider = a1["rider_id"]
    # Explicit /dispatch — should target the OTHER rider since the first holds OFFERED.
    s, b = CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/dispatch",
                          role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="admin")
    assert s == 201, (s, b)
    a2_id = b["data"]["id"]
    a2 = STORE.assignments[a2_id]
    assert a2["rider_id"] != first_rider, (a2, first_rider)
    # Both rider1 and rider2 should now hold offers.
    offers = [a for a in STORE.assignments.values()
              if a["order_id"] == o["id"] and a["status"] == "OFFERED"]
    assert len(offers) == 2, offers
    # No third dispatch is possible — pool is now empty.
    s, b = CLIENT.request("POST", f"/api/orders/{o['id']}/dispatch",
                          role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="admin")
    assert s == 409 and b["data"]["error_id"] == "ERR_INVALID_STATE", (s, b)
